text: Harbour City takes an early lead near their own left flank around 13 metres from the opposing goal with Elias Okafor scoring after a patient 17-pass build-up, assisted by Marek Barros [#905]. Barros quickly doubles the lead for Harbour City from the right flank at about 44 metres, sending a long-range cross into the net shortly after halftime [#975]. Seabrook Town responds at their right wing near the opposition’s 10-metre mark through Tariq Marlowe’s quick strike from regained possession [#1104]. After tactical changes, Seabrook Town presses higher and plays more directly, culminating in Callum Varga cutting in from the right flank around 9 metres from goal to score [#1448]. In injury time, Kian Romano first equalizes at the left side, close to the six-metre box, assisted by Aiden Quinlan [#1882]. Moments later, Romano scores again from a short pass near the centre-right area at three metres, completing a late turnaround and sealing a 4-2 victory for Seabrook Town [#1906]. Marek Barros stands out with 1 goal, 2 assists, and 9 interceptions despite Harbour City’s defeat.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for audio audience in en

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with a total xG of 3.44, dominating shots (22) and shots on target (9) compared to Harbour City's 2 goals and 1.03 xG [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Harbour City led early with goals at 45' and 47' by Elias Okafor and Marek Barros but lost the advantage after Seabrook Town’s goals starting at 53' [#905, #975, #1104].
- Kian Romano scored twice in injury time (90+2' and 90+3'), securing Seabrook Town’s comeback victory [#1882, #1906].
- Seabrook Town maintained higher possession (53.4%) and field tilt (57.7%) overall, with 60 box touches versus Harbour City's 41 [team_stats].
- Marek Barros was player of the match despite being on the losing side, with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and highest rating 9.8 [player_of_the_match].

- Harbour City, playing a 4-2-3-1 with a patient short passing style, built their first half goal through a prolonged 17-pass sequence over nearly a minute, showing their preference for sustained possession and methodical buildup before Elias Okafor scored from a through ball assist by Marek Barros [#904,905].
- Marek Barros notably combined a quick cross from a corner situation into a long-range goal shortly after halftime, indicating that Harbour City could capitalize on set pieces and utilize their wide players to break the 3-4-3 defensive structure of Seabrook Town [#973,975].
- Seabrook Town’s 3-4-3 formation with wide crossing play led to multiple scoring chances; their first goal by Tariq Marlowe came immediately after a ball regain, suggesting effective pressing and quick transition to attack exploiting the spaces left by Harbour City’s 4-2-3-1 when pushing forward [#1103,1104].
- After going behind, Seabrook Town’s coach instructed tactical changes including higher pressing, increased directness, and higher defensive line height, which helped them regain momentum, win duels higher up the pitch, and create big chances, culminating in three late goals through a mix of direct play and through balls exploiting Harbour City’s defensive line [#1361,1447,1881,1882].
